en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Master Ying’an:
The Way cannot be transmitted through words; it cannot be understood through sentiment; it cannot be cognized by consciousness.
If this is so, then what use are the Recorded Sayings of Ying’an? Since ancient times, there have never been venerable masters who remained silent. As...
To stop a child’s crying with yellow leaves is to sever the extremes of the middle and the periphery and transcend the three periods of time;

this is called investigating the "live word," which cannot be understood by those who merely study the literal language. That later generations take these teachings as their model is what is meant by being "imperishable.
This is why Master Ying’an could not remain silent and simply let it be. Recently, the Master hung up his staff at Tiantai Huguo Temple, acting as...
He was praised by Yuan Budai, who invited him to serve as the First Seat (Dìyīzuò). He stood out prominently like a wild crane emerging from a flock of chickens.
From that time on, his reputation spread far and wide throughout all quarters. In the Bingzi year of the Shaoxing era, when I was leaving the commandery for Sanqu, I encountered him on the road.
We stayed briefly at Baituo Temple, where we conversed until the end of the night; our debate was so versatile and profound that it was like a great river flowing eastward.
Commentary: "Rolling on and on, there is no end to be known. It is like driving a light carriage along a familiar path, traveling through the four quarters without hindrance or obstruction.
For this reason, it was expected that this master would surely be able to revitalize the single lineage of Yangqi. Later, he indeed resided extensively at famous mountains;

wherever he went, the assembly of cloud-robed monks (monks) accorded him great respect. Finally, his dharma seat at Tiantong was especially flourishing, with people shoulder-to-shoulder and sleeve-to-sleeve.
They were interconnected; according to their respective capacities, all who heard the Dharma obtained something of benefit.
Furthermore, among those who emerged with outstanding brilliance, Xianzhong Quan, once he resided at Fengshan, compiled the Master’s lifetime teachings into a single volume.

To transmit this to future students, his resolve may indeed be deemed diligent. As the saying goes, "One discerns the soil from the sprouts; one recognizes a person through their speech," this record cannot be dispensed with.

Yet, viewed through the correct eye (*samyag-dṛṣṭi*), even if one were as swift as a pearl rolling upon a tray or as chaotic as falling flowers in the sky, it would still not constitute seeing the principle of Ying’an.
This matter is truly difficult to deliberate upon; for those who possess the will [to seek the truth], [this record is essential].
It is fitting that this be rendered with brilliance; then the Master’s words and deeds will surely be propagated. Preface by the Layman Songchuang, Qian Duanli.

Having received the Master’s kind instruction: "A single phrase, free from self-interest, benefits sentient beings. The Master said, "Only by knowing gratitude can one understand how to repay it.
He continued, "Last night a pure breeze arose across the eight directions; this morning the flowing waters swell the stream before the cliff. The Master said:
"A wind-chasing heavenly horse wearing a qilin. The monk stepped forward and said, "Not only does the Left Assistant (the Master) receive this goodness;
I, your student, prostrate to thank you for your kindness. The Master said, "I have not yet let you go. The monk prostrated. The Master said, "You have lost it beneath your heels."
The Master then said: "A precious sword brandished in the void leaves heaven and earth devoid of luster. It overturns the nest of right and wrong and cuts off the very roots of birth and death.
Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; thus, earth and heaven endure for eternity. Where there is no Buddha, one must pass swiftly by; thus, the rivers are clear and the seas are calm.
A single phrase held in its entirety beyond three thousand miles—there is not even a hair’s breadth of leakage. Such a one is fit to be a Buddha."
The Patriarch acted as a teacher, creating a model for gods and humans. At such a time, how do you express the phrase "transforming the mundane into the sacred"?
Do you understand? "The moon in the empty expanse of the ten-thousand-year-old blue pool—only after repeated scooping and searching will you finally come to know it."
Ascending the hall upon entering the monastery, a monk asked: "Having departed from Kuangxiao and come to attend at Miaoyan, what is the Venerable One of Immovability?
The Master said: "Five days' journey since we parted at Liancheng. The monk stepped forward and said: "Though the bamboo is dense, it does not hinder the flowing stream;

though the mountain is high, how could it obstruct the soaring white clouds? The Master said: "This old monk has never moved a step. The monk said: "Today I have been fortunate enough to hear this..."

[The monk] said, “I have not heard it. The Master said, “You must spit it out immediately! [The monk] stepped forward and said, “Yangqi in days past; the Master today. The Master said, “There is no place for you here.
[The monk] stepped forward and said, “How can one deny that this public case is already established? The Master said, “I thought you were a man of substance.
The monk said, “Zha! (A note of realization). The Master said, “Not yet. The Master then said: “A solitary peak ten thousand fathoms high; a bird’s path, empty and profound.”

Fame and profit are utterly forgotten; right and wrong are suddenly severed. It reaches the point where monkeys howl among ancient trees and tigers roar from secluded crags—this is the livelihood of the Way-man amidst the azure void and blue heavens.
Although it is thus, you must further know that there is a "higher aperture" wherein both man and environment are simultaneously stripped away.
[The Master] then raises his whisk and says: "The stars in heaven all bow toward the North; among men, no water flows but toward the East."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet it is difficult to behold within those very eyes.
If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, and speech. Yet when speech and action are employed, there is no point of contact.
Where, then, does the true essence of the Great Way reside? After a long silence, he said: "How pitiable is Master Fu! Everywhere he goes, he loses his pavilion."

Emerging from the ranks to return to the hall, one penetrates through iron walls and silver mountains. Amidst the clamor of the dusty marketplace, the ancient Buddha’s家风 (family style) is fully revealed.
Passing through wine shops and tea houses, one brings forth the very core of the patch-robed monk.
One coldly laughs at those everywhere who are like cold ashes and withered wood, sitting in a place of soullessness and certain death. Miaoyan possesses a measure of spiritual power for all of you.
He lets out a breath. He plants his staff and says, "For thirty years I have been riding a horse, yet I was instead given a prediction by a blind donkey.
He plants the staff once more and descends from the seat.

[The Master] ascends the hall and says: "Sitting in face-to-the-wall meditation for nine years ruined the descendants in this land of China; returning to the West with a single shoe left the Yellow-Faced One frustrated."
Laozi. He struck once with his staff and said: "The stone ox guards the ancient path; one horse gives birth to three tigers.
He ascended the hall and said: "Old woman Huangbo, talkative Dagu: there is not much to this Buddha-dharma; the blind donkey of the true eye has been extinguished."
Suddenly he picked up his staff and said, "Miaoyan suddenly emerges; the three men take a tortoise and certify it as a softshell turtle.
He struck the ground once with the staff and said, "This staff is skilled at discerning; stiffen your backbone and do not let it leak out.
Guanyin Bodhisattva buys a sesame cake with money, but when he puts it down, it turns out to be a piece of raw iron. Thereupon, he threw down the staff.
Descend from your seats.
Ascend the hall. A man of great capacity must fiercely shatter all former wiles; he must cut straight through like a nail driven home or iron severed.
He must cast aside the devices of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and pull out the hitching post for the donkey. Have you not seen how Muzhou was too intimate with people?
Yunmen was pressed until his feet broke; later, his descendants failed to discern the essential point and instead sought to distinguish it at the very place where the door is pushed open.
If you practice Chan in such a manner, you will not find rest for donkey years. Wuyuan, not sparing a single hair on my brow, shall extract it for you right from the start.
Suddenly seizing his staff and casting it down, he said: "The people of Jambudvīpa are always in the north."
At Utpalavati, he ascended the hall.
He cited a monk who asked Da-sui, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master? Sui said, "Painting a winnowing basket with red earth.
The monk asked, "What is painting a winnowing basket with red earth? Sui said, "The winnowing basket has lips; the rice leaps out."
[The Master] comes forth. The Master says: "Do you all know where Da-sui has fallen? Miaoyan shall further express this in verse:
'The winnowing basket has a lip; the rice cannot leap out. All the monks under heaven are bare-boned [of realization]; one must still turn back the uppermost barrier.'"
The worlds of the ten directions are as black as lacquer. [With this, he] struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [he said]: "In the forest of thorns, there is crimson rot; on the back of a broken donkey, there are flies.

As for those who preside over the court like Han Xin, or the Buddha of Dongshan who has no light—this whole crew! They strike three thousand blows at dawn and eight hundred blows at dusk. What crime have they committed?"
[The Master] said, "It is past. Suppose a copper bowl were filled to the brim with oil; how would you all handle it?
After a long silence, he said, "A large month has thirty days; a small month has twenty-nine."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Xuansha asked Jingqing, "Not seeing a single dharma is a great affliction. He then asked, "Tell me, what dharma do you not see?
Jingqing pointed to a pillar and said, "Is it not this very dharma?
Xuansha replied, "In Zhejiang, you may have clear water and white rice to eat, but as for the Buddha-dharma, you have not seen it even in your dreams. The Master said, "Jingqing was being stubborn."
Even the Buddhas and Patriarchs could do nothing about it. Had it not been for Xuansha’s profound discernment of the "wind" [of the situation], he would have nearly been swallowed by a pillar.
If there is anyone who can discern this, I shall entrust both hands to Miaoyan.
Ascending the hall: At the tips of the hundred grasses, the weapons of war are laid to rest; before the ten-thousand-fathom peaks, one plays freely and at will.
One sighs in secret over Lu-zu facing the wall, who was single-mindedly addicted to nothing but sleep; yet one laughs instead at Mu-zhou seeing a monk and saying, "Bring me a bucket of water.
At such a time, even Linji’s shout like a thunderous rush is set aside, as is Deshan’s staff.
Like scattering stars, he likewise placed them all in one spot. Miaoyan had a single living path for you all to walk together;
he then drew a circle and said: "The one on the left side of the foot of the eastern mountain."
Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bathing ceremony, a monk asked: "The Old Man with the Yellow Face has a case that remains unresolved from two thousand years ago;
I ask the Master to provide a critical judgment on it for him. The Master said: "Looking up, one does not see the sky; looking down, one does not see the earth. The monk pressed further:
"If the Patriarch could not resolve it, the trouble will surely reach his descendants. The Master said: "Do not slander him. The monk continued: "Since..."
“This is the pure Dharmakāya; fundamentally, it has no appearing or disappearing. Why do you year after year splash foul water upon it?

The Master said, “I want him to know pain and itching. [The student] further asked, “As for Great Master Yunmen saying, ‘If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him with one blow and fed him to a dog,’ what kind of eyes did he possess? The Master said, “The entire great earth.”
No one knows where it has fallen. A student stepped forward and said, "Although Master Yunmen sat in total command of heaven and earth, how could he avoid falling into the trap of old Śākyamuni?
The Master said, "The thief is caught as a thief. The Master then continued: "Deshan tore down the Buddha hall;
Yunmen struck him dead with a single blow. As for 'Three pounds of flax,' that is what is inside the hall. Beneath the Bamboo Grove Mountain..."
His sinews were lashed; he suffered three strokes of the painful staff and arrived at Dongshan nine times. If you try to deliberate this as a matter of Buddha-dharma, your tongue will rot away;
if you do not deliberate it as a matter of Buddha-dharma, you will fall into pits and ditches. Arriving here, with this black lacquer staff, there is grievance but no place to cry out.
Though the incense burner in the ancient temple is cold, it will burn the *śrāmaṇera* to death. At such a time as this, what is it? Wuling.
Spring has already grown old; the terraces and pavilions are filled with lush green shade.
Ascending the hall, he takes up his staff and says: "In the past, the venerable master Baiyun End said:

'When the ancients left behind a single word or half a phrase, if one had not yet penetrated it, it was as if one had run into an iron wall. Suddenly, one day, after seeing through it, one finally realizes for oneself...'"
"One's own self is already an iron wall. Tell me, how do you penetrate it now? He then said, "Iron wall, iron wall.
The Master struck the ground once with his staff and said, "Iron wall, iron wall. Swiftly, as by the imperial decree of the *liùlìng* (magical command). He then descended from his seat.
The Recorded Sayings of Mingguo Chan Monastery at Tongsan, Quzhou, Compiled by Dharma Heirs (Shouquan), etc. Entering the Monastery for the Opening of the Hall.
Holding up the incense, he said: "This one offering of incense is respectfully [offered] for..."
"May His Majesty the Emperor enjoy a long life—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years! Next, he picks up incense and says:
"I reverently offer this incense for the Chancellor, the Secretariat Drafter, the two Circuit Intendants, and all the civil and military officials of the entire prefecture.

May their ranks and emoluments increase and flourish. Again, picking up incense, he says: "This one portion of incense is offered for the former abbot of Zhangjiao in Xuanzhou, who later resided at..."
Venerable Master Long of Yunyan Chan Monastery at Mount Huqiu in Pingjiang burns incense in the burner to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk.
Let the monks of the world do as they please—beating bricks and striking tiles. Thereupon, the Master adjusted his robes and took his seat.
After Venerable Master Xuedang of Mount Wugu struck the mallet, the Master said: "To realize the emptiness of the primary truth is called the Lion’s Roar. The Master...
Once the lion has roared, the foxes and wolves hide their tracks and those of other species vanish; is there anyone here who can step forward from beneath his paws?
Come forth and meet him! A monk asked: "When Deshan enters the gate and immediately strikes with his staff, that is a vajra-ring.
When Linji enters the gate and immediately shouts, that is a vajra-ring. But as for Muzhou seeing a monk and saying, 'A fellow carrying a board,' what is that?"
"What is it? The Master said, "It is a lump of iron. The monk asked, "If someone were to say it is a *liji* (thorny) plum, what then?
The Master said, "Sticking one's head into a vat of glue. The monk said, "From of old, no one has recognized the sweat-poured horses."
"If one were to re-examine his epoch-making merit," the Master said, "it is nine times nine equals eighty-one. The Master then continued:

"Those who are adept with words speak that which cannot be spoken; those who are adept with traces leave traces that cannot be traced. When both words and traces are exhausted," [the truth is revealed].
This is still merely an adaptation according to principle; it is not yet sufficient to behold the true splendor within the gate of the Zen monk.

Therefore, from the Buddhas and Patriarchs of old, the seal of correctness was upheld and the essential purport was secretly transmitted. Without possessing the great eye that distinguishes black from white, how could one hope to reach such heights?
Have you not seen how the World-Honored One, beneath the Bodhi tree, attained Perfect Enlightenment when the morning star appeared?
At that time, all sentient beings of the great earth attained and realized [this] together. For forty-nine years, he exhausted every bit of his compassionate "old woman’s heart.
Finally, before a great assembly of a million people, he held up a flower; only Mahākāśyapa smiled, whereupon [the Buddha] said:
"I have the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the Wondrous Mind of Nirvāṇa; I now entrust it to Mahākāśyapa. I dare ask you all: Furthermore—
The Way involves either being entrusted with it or not being entrusted with it. If one says there is an entrustment, then one buries one’s elder brother Kāśyapa.
If one says there is no entrustment, then one fails Śākyamuni the Old Man.

Here, if the distinction between the Jing and the Wei rivers is not made, then the entrustment at Vulture Peak becomes a mere empty formality. At this very moment, is there anyone who can speak? If you...
"If you can explain it, the price of this fruit will increase tenfold. If you cannot, then only after the snow has fallen does one know the steadfastness of the pine and cypress;

only when faced with difficulty is the heart of a true man revealed. He raised another case: When Baoshou opened the hall for his first sermon, Sansheng pushed forward a monk. Baoshou struck him immediately.
Sansheng said, "If you act as a teacher in this manner, you will blind the people of the entire city of Zhenzhou! Baoshou...

Baoshou threw down his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters. The Master said, "In the monastic communities, everyone debates this, saying that Baoshou and Sansheng were masterful smelters and wielded the authentic tongs and hammers. What connection does this have?
Little do they realize that these two elders were pinned down by this monk, and even until today, they cannot be raised up. Is there anyone here today who can clear their names?"
"Qudima, come forth and meet Mingguo. Is there anyone here? He suddenly picked up his staff, threw it down, and said, "It is easy to distinguish dragons from snakes;
it is difficult to deceive a patch-robed monk."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Mihu instructed a monk to ask Yangshan, "Do people of the present day still require awakening?
Yangshan replied, "Awakening is not non-existent, but alas, it falls into the second place. When the monk returned and reported this to Mihu, Mihu deeply approved of it. The Master said:
"Mihu wielded the hammer of one's own fundamental share, while Yangshan displayed his skill on the edge of the sword. These two elders—"

Within the gate of proclaiming the teachings, he is certainly worthy of being called venerable; yet, within the school of the patch-robed monks, he is nothing but a fellow who deserves a blow of the staff.
Entering the hall: Nine, nine, nine. Old Śākyamuni did not know there was more to it; turning his face around, he extends his hairy hand.
Gripping the vajra hammer, he shatters the old molds; the True Person of No Rank stands out in bold relief. Each and every one looks south to see the Northern Dipper.
[The Master] descends from the seat.
Ascending the hall for the Buddha-Bathing ceremony: When the Elder Śākyamuni was first born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth.

"In heaven above and on earth below, I alone am honored. Later, Yunmen said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to a dog, just to ensure peace in the world. The Master said, "Although this story of Yunmen is widely circulated..."
"He cannot avoid falling into another's trap. The Old Man with the Yellow Face finally sells his wares; this is truly 'clinging to grass and clinging to wood,' and neither side is resolved.
Striking the meditation seat with his left hand, he said: "Go over here! Do you all see where Mingguo has fallen?
Two rows of tears upon the coral pillow—half are for thinking of you, half are for hating you."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "The Chan Master Dahui said that the single word 'no' is the blade that cuts off birth and death.
Is this truly so, or not? The Master said, "To speak in such a manner, you have not yet dreamed of Zhaozhou.
The monk pressed further, "If someone were suddenly to ask the Master, 'Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? how would you respond? The Master said, "No, monk."
[The Master] prostrated and then raised the case. A monk asked Yunmen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still transgression?
Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru. The Master said: "Yunmen’s answer was indeed correct and precise, yet it ultimately fell into the secondary position.
If Mingguo were alive today, he would not have answered so. Suppose someone were to ask him: 'If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still transgression? He would simply—"
He addressed the assembly: "Bring forth a question.

On the occasion of the Imperial Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "The First Principle of the Holy Truth is lofty and unsurpassed; it is vast and boundless. It is profound and bottomless; it is deep and unfathomable.
Heaven and earth rely upon it for their covering and supporting; the sun and moon rely upon it for their shining and presiding. It is empty..."
Space is vast because it relies upon this; the myriad spirits attain transformation and adaptability because they rely upon this.

Therefore, I, a man of the way beneath the forest trees, rely upon this to study the dharma of non-action and awaken to the patience of non-arising. But tell me: how do you express the single phrase of repaying the debt of gratitude?
A burner of agarwood incense and a single recitation of the Buddha’s name—this I offer in homage to my Master.
May the Emperor live for ten million years.

Grand Marshal Han ascended the hall and raised up the account of Military Commissioner Zhu entering Nanji Temple, where he took the hand of a monk from the Qi dynasty as he walked while holding an incense burner.
He then said: "Right here! Right here! At that time, a monk asked: "What is it right here? Zhu—
The military commander Xingjun said in verse: "A monk is one who practices the Buddha-dharma; why do you give rise to anger?
The monk asked, "Do you take 'giving rise to anger' to mean that I am committing evil? The monk then shouted, and Xingjun also shouted, saying, "The hook is in the place of non-suspicion.
He then called to his attendants, "Identify this monk! The Master said: "Xingjun drew forth his sky-relying long sword, while this monk..."
"Opening one's breast, one dares to charge at the edge of a snow-white blade. Although neither harms the other, alas, both are playing with danger.

Today, when the Imperial Commissioner, the Grand Marshal, entered the mountains to offer alms to monks, although there was no such exchange of words, you must know that this story has already been set in motion."
This story having been circulated, tell me: what was it that was said? "When the Sleeping Dragon first exerts his power, the Vermilion Phoenix soars as well.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "The Buddhas of the three periods have no sinews in their eyes; the Patriarchs of the six generations have no blood under their skin.
Mingguo bites down on his teeth with determination; even if he were to leap about, he could not escape from his own trap. Why is this? Because Nanquan slaughtered the cat."
Ascending the hall: A thousand streams have cold waters; ten thousand ravines have frosty clouds. The "True Person of No Rank" is a dried-up dung pellet;
the Vajra Jewel Sword shatters the sturdy barrier. The almanac of many years is most efficacious; look closely at the tip of the hundred-foot pole. Blind the eyes and silence the mouth;
iron hammers without holes march in a procession. Now, as for that one phrase behind the head—what rank of function is it?
[The Master] gave a shout and said: "In the Yaśas Stūpa, they strike the iron chime; at Tiantai and Yandang, human traffic is cut off.
He then raised the case of Zhaozhou visiting Zhunyu. Upon reaching the Dharma Hall, Zhaozhou walked from east to west and from west to east.
Zhunyu asked, "What are you doing? Zhaozhou replied, "I am testing the water. Zhunyu said, "There isn't even a single drop here. What are you testing? Zhaozhou—
Leaning his staff against the wall, he went out. The Master said, "Zhu-yu does not have even a single drop; there is only white waves flooding the heavens.
Zhaozhou leaned his staff against the wall and did not stir a ripple. Although these two elders shared the same death and the same life, how could Mingguo bear to let them go?
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Nan-yuan addressed the assembly, saying, "Upon this lump of red flesh, ten thousand fathoms stand sheer.
A monk came forward and said, "Upon this lump of red flesh, ten thousand fathoms stand sheer—is this not the Master’s own words? Nan-yuan said, "Yes. The monk then overturned the meditation seat.
Nan-yuan said, "You blind fellow! and struck him. The Master remarked, "This too is like inviting a thief to ruin one's house; had it not been for..."
This monk dares to pull at the tiger’s whiskers. Who would not see that Nan-yuan’s merit from his war-horses is high? Nevertheless, Mingguo provides yet another path:
upon this ball of red flesh, it stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. If a monk comes forth, he should strike him across the spine. Why?
"The sword that kills, the blade that gives life—those with eyes, look!
He ascends the hall and says: "Upon the cliffs of Shaoshi, the wind blows and the rocks split; before the Hall of Great Penetration, cold ashes burst like beans.
A man of great character cuts through both ends with a single stroke. Suddenly seizing his staff, he says: "Do you all know Mingguo’s staff?"
"Ma. After a long silence, he taps the meditation seat once and says: "When the dragon gains water, its spirit increases; when the tiger encounters mountain scenery, its fierce majesty grows.
He ascends the hall and cites the verse of Master Xiu: "Two broken do not constitute one; the One Dharma eternally endures. If one acts...
"Meeting once or twice, one will suffer in the depths of saṃsāra for eternal kalpas. The Master said, "This would mean sitting and killing Master Xiushan.
Even if you do not meet him once or twice, you cannot avoid entering the womb of a donkey or a horse.

You people here—during the twelve periods of the day, in walking, standing, sitting, and lying down—do you know where to let go of body and life? Have you not heard it said: 'If not the south of the River, then the north of the River'?"
[The Master] lets out a shout. He descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he cites the case of Muzhou asking a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk immediately shouts. Muzhou says, "I, this old monk, have been shouted at by you.
The monk shouts again. Muzhou says, "After three or four shouts, what then? The monk is speechless. Muzhou then strikes him.
This is a hollow, empty braggart. The Master said: "In the monastic communities, people speculate, saying: 'When he has finished those three or four shouts, what then?
They say one should immediately overturn the meditation seat; otherwise, drag away the sitting mat and strike him across the mouth;
otherwise, shake out the sleeves and depart; or else, give him another shout. To speak in such a manner and yet claim to be a descendant of Bodhidharma—how could that be?"
"Far away. [The Master] went to the meditation hall. He descended from his seat. He ascended the hall. He raised the case:
A monk asked Yunmen, "If one kills one's father and mother, one repents before the Buddha. But if one kills the Buddha and the Patriarchs, where does one repent?
Yunmen said, "Exposed! The Master said, "Yunmen’s 'Exposed' is as fierce as a tiger. Master Bodhidharma..."
"It is not the Patriarch. Have you not seen it? The old man of Yanguan takes Mount Sumeru as his mallet and empty space as his drum. And have you not seen it?
The old man of Heishan knows how to beat the drum—do not be so crude! A sweet melon is sweet to the very stem; a bitter gourd is bitter to the very root.
With a shout, he descended from the seat.
When Master Xuetang of Wugushan arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "Linji, having received three painful blows, realized his homecoming at Gaoyuan Rapids.
At Da'jue's staff, Xinghua deeply clarified the intent of Huangbo. Brothers of the mountains..."

Although we are few in number, each of us is afflicted by a malady deep within the vital organs. Had it not been for the arrival of you, Venerable Shishu, how would Mingguo have dared to venture to convey this news?
Shortly after descending from the seat, I shall join the various administrative officers, heads of departments, and the assembly in extending our formal invitation.
We humbly beseech your compassion and earnestly pray that you will administer the necessary medicine to cure us.
Ascending the hall: Ten thousand *li* without a blade of grass; the blue sky resounds with a clap of thunder. The deluded fellow at the crossroads cannot be struck dead by the staff;
Xie Sanlang on the fishing boat has always been selling "qiao. Whether there is a phrase or no phrase, it is like a vine leaning against a tree;
when the tree falls, the vine withers. Guishan laughs heartily—tell me, what matter does he clarify? The power of Yu...
"Reaching nowhere; the sound of the river flows toward the west.
[The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks, "What is it like when empty space is exhausted? The Master says, "Where Li Lou walks, the waves overflow the heavens."
Again, it is recounted: Xuefeng, Yantou, and Qingshan studied under Deshan. Qingshan asked, "Tianhuang spoke thus; Longtan also spoke thus.
I wonder, Master, how would you speak? Deshan said, "Try citing Tianhuang’s and Longtan’s words for me.
As Qingshan hesitated, Deshan struck him. Having been struck, Qingshan returned to Yan.
Shou Tang said, "It is so, it is so—but you have struck me far too hard. Yan Tou said, "If you act like this, you will not be able to say later that you saw Deshan.
Xuedou commented, "Qinshan established this point of inquiry; how extraordinary! Yet, alas, he was headstrong but tailless.
You should try citing the cases of Tian Huang and Long Tan: [Tian Huang] simply struck his sitting cloth, and [Long Tan] said, 'A great man!'"
In the Han dynasty, it was one’s duty to pull at the tiger’s whiskers.

Since he [Shishuang] could not cause Deshan’s command to be carried out even half-way, had he been able to carry out the command in its entirety, Xuefeng and Yantou would both have been men of the Nirvana Hall. The Master said:

"If a patriarch did not possess the eye that penetrates the barrier and the mechanism beyond the ordinary, how could he distinguish between black and white at the moment of extending his hand? It is just like this:"
Deshan ordered that half be carried out; did Xuedou manage to escape it?
Since he could not escape, had he passed beneath Deshan’s gate at that time, he would have been one who ate the staff. [Xuedou] suddenly picks up his staff and says, "Do you see Deshan?
He then strikes the ground once with it and says, "The thief is the petty man."

On the first day of the month, Master Yue Dan ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "Three days before and five days after—if one does not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in the trees.
Mingguo had a turning phrase for this; he wished for everyone to know it together: "The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horns because it gazes at the moon;
the elephant has flowers enter its tusks because it is startled by thunder. He then descended from his seat.
The Record of Sayings of Chan Master Dechang Anguo of Qizhou, compiled by his Dharma heirs (Shouquan), etc. Entering the Monastery;
Ascending the Dharma Seat. A monk asked: "The faculty does not depart from its station. I do not ask about the stilling of the faculty when it is in use; I wonder, however, regarding the myriad..."
"How can one communicate where the spiritual capacity does not reach? The Master said, "One instance, forty-nine. The student advanced and said, "He sits and cuts off the ten directions.
The Master said, "Do you want to make this old monk mute? The student said, "What kind of mental activity is the Master's?
The Master said, "What kind of mental activity is yours? The student said, "Right here, it still involves this one..."
The student asked, "Can these sentences be attained? The Master said, "One can attain a thousand or ten thousand sentences.

The student further asked, "As for the place where the myriad functions do not reach, how does one travel there? The Master said, "In the place where the myriad functions do not reach, there are seven openings and eight holes.

The student asked, "How can one cope with being utterly naked and without support, completely bare and fully exposed? The Master said, "That is the place where you, Venerable Sir, gain strength. The student pressed on.
[The Master] said: "It is just like when a monk asked Xiangyan, 'When one does not admire the various sages and does not prize one's own spiritual essence, what then?
Xiangyan replied, 'All myriad functions cease; even the thousand sages cannot carry it. Shushan—what kind of eyes and brain did he have that he would not accept Xiangyan?"
The Master said, "Your defeat, *ācārya*, is becoming increasingly complete. The student asked, "If one neither accepts nor assents, has one still clarified the meaning of Xiangyan?
The Master said, "I would have your tongue rot away. The student asked, "To accept is to accept those other sages;
to assent is to assent to one's own spiritual nature. Yet Xiangyan did not accept Shushan—how can this be explained? The Master said, "On level ground."
[The monk] ate and left. Later, he went to Jingqing and asked: "Shushan previously said that 'affirmation and negation cannot be total. How should a practitioner handle this? Jingqing replied:
"'Total' is itself affirmation and negation. The monk asked: "What is the principle behind this? The Master said: "You have lost your staff. The monk lifted up his sitting cloth and said:
"What can be done about this? The Master said: "You have mistaken the zero-point on the scale. The monk then said: "Shushan..."

"The Way cannot be fully grasped. Furthermore, what is it like? Qing said, "Within this, there is no path of acquiescence. "Does one still attain the crown and the base? The Master said, "Seeing the cheek from behind the head.
The student advanced and asked, "When a student does not maintain acquiescence and does not establish a 'yes,' how is it then?
The Master said, "Rolling in the grass. The student said, "Let it roll as far as the heavens; I will not bury it in the earth. The Master—
[The Master] said, "It is still a bit lacking. The monk bowed. The Master said, "To get a donkey and be so happy!
Then the Master took up his staff and said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time were like this; the six generations of patriarchs were also like this."
The old monk of the world is also like this. Zhangshan further adds feet to a snake for everyone.
He strikes the meditation seat once and says: "Ten thousand functions are all stilled; a single arrow hits the red heart. He then raises another case:
Under the assembly of Jia Shan, there was a monk who went to Gao Ting. As soon as he prostrated himself, Ting struck him across the spine. The monk said, "Master, do not strike me!"
Again, when the monk prostrated, Gao Ting struck him again and drove him out. The monk reported this to Jia Shan. Shan asked, "Do you understand?
The monk said, "I do not understand. Shan said, "Fortunately you do not understand. If you had understood, Jia Shan’s mouth would have been closed for good.
The Master said: "Gao Ting could not restrain his impatience for a moment; yet, how could he help it that the staff let go too quickly? If that monk had, at that time..."
This fellow—let alone Gao Ting or Jia Shan; even if Bodhidharma himself were to appear, he would cut him into three pieces. Why?
Because when the family prospers, filial sons are born; when the state is hegemonic, there are strategic ministers.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Before the peak of Shaoshi, the 'lacquer bucket' story has fallen; on the road to Caoxi, you have been deceived, O *śrāmaṇeras*.
Have any of you ever seen this in a dream? Have you not heard it said: 'A field of a thousand years has eight hundred owners;
a gnat swallows a tiger'? He then cited the case: Linji asked the temple steward, "Where have you come from? The steward replied, "From the Prefecture."
Ji was selling yellow millet from within [the hall]. He used his staff to draw a line and said, "Can you sell this?
The host (the abbot) gave a shout; Ji struck him. Next, the head cook arrived. Ji presented the same matter to the head cook. The cook said, "The Hall Master does not understand the Master's meaning.
Ji used his staff to draw a line and asked, "And what about you? The cook bowed. Ji [struck him].
He struck him again. Master Nanyuan of Huanglong commented: "When the head of the monastery shouted, he could not have let it pass;
when the cook prostrated, letting it pass was impossible. Linji’s command was being carried out. Guizong let it pass, and thirty years later someone explained it through.
Master Daopei Zhe commented: "The head of the monastery shouted; the cook prostrated; Linji’s command was being carried out."

"Unrivaled throughout past and present," the Master said. "Though these two old fellows strove mightily to uphold the fundamental principles of our school, when scrutinized, they could not avoid merely 'clinging to the grass and leaning on the wood.
Little did they realize that both Linji, the Great and the Small, had their homes destroyed and their dwellings scattered by these two fellows.
Do you understand? This is the sword that kills and the sword that gives life."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: When Master Fuyong first visited Guizong, he asked, "What is the Buddha?
Guizong said, "I will tell you; do you believe me? Fuyong replied, "Since these are the words of the Honored One, how could I dare not believe?

Guizong said, "It is you yourself. Fuyong asked, "How does one maintain this? Guizong said, "A single film over the eye causes empty flowers to fall in confusion. Dharma-Eye (Fayan) took up this case.
He said, "If Guizong had no 'afterword,' what would there be to call him Guizong?
Fayan spoke thus, which is truly like a blind man feeling an elephant. Then, picking up his staff, he said, "Do you all wish to see where Zhangshan acts for others?
He threw it down and said, "Thirty years hence."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an old case: A monk asked Yangshan, "Does the Dharma-body understand how to preach the Dharma?
Yangshan said, "I cannot preach it; there is another person who can preach it. The monk asked, "Where is he right now? Yangshan then pushed out his pillow and showed it to him.
Guishan said, "Ji-zi (Yangshan) employs matters from the edge of a sword. The Master said, "If it were a matter from the edge of a sword..."
When did Yangshan ever truly understand how to apply this? Once, when a monk came forward and asked Changshan, "Does the Dharma-body know how to preach the Dharma?
he replied to him, "I cannot say it; there is another who can.
He was then asked, "Where is that person who can say it? To which he simply responded, "Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Baizhang, "What is the extraordinary matter? Baizhang said, "Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak.
The monk bowed, and Baizhang struck him. The Master remarked, "Great Baizhang! His answer was incomplete."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: After the Sixth Patriarch had received the Dharma, he passed by Faxing Temple and sat among the corridors.
One evening, as the wind blew the banner atop the pagoda, two monks engaged in debate. One said, "The wind moves"; the other said, "The banner moves. They argued back and forth without end.
The Sixth Patriarch asked, "May I, a mere layman, venture to join in such a lofty discussion? The two monks replied, "We wish to hear your interpretation. The Patriarch said:
"It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving. It is your mind, O virtuous one, that moves. The Master commented: "One blind man leads a crowd of blind men;
together they are dragged into a pit of fire."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Old blind baldy De-zhang has never had a single taste. He picks up his mouth and loses his nose;
at two o'clock in the third watch, he sings a folk song, needlessly startling the sleep of Brahmā. With a shout, he says: 'I walk through the wild weeds;
you, in turn, enter the deep village.'"
The Recorded Sayings of Master Ying’an, Volume One;
The Recorded Sayings of Master Ying’an, Volume Two:
The Record of the Raoyang Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Monastery.
Compiled by the Dharma-heirs (Shouquan) and others.
The Master entered the abbot’s quarters, took his seat, and said: "This is a case of immediate realization; it cuts off all confusion. To provide a mistaken commentary would break your back.
To lift the robe and walk away is a terminal illness. One must be a man of exceptional talent to have a different way of life. Suddenly—
When encountering the rushing cloud-fleeted hawk, what is it like when it arrives? A net spread across the heavens in hundreds of thousands of layers.
Entering the hall, [the Master] raised the matter of Linji’s intent in receiving the staff three times under Huangbo:
"Have you all yet seen through this? Even if one were to bite through it at once, such a person would still not be a true man of great character. The three periods of time...
"The Buddhas hang their mouths on the wall. What will the old monks of the world use to eat?
He ascended the hall and cited the teaching of Salt Officer (Yanguan), who said to the assembly: "Taking empty space as a drum and Mount Sumeru as a mallet—what person can beat it?
The assembly was speechless. Nanquan said, "Old Wang does not beat this broken drum. Fayan said, "Old Wang..."
The Master did not strike him. The Master said, "Those two venerable elders were much like those who eat plums but bite only the skin.
Today, Baoyuan goes to meet Yanguan: taking empty space as the drum and Mount Sumeru as the mallet, if he is to strike, he strikes—do not ask who it is.
He suddenly picked up his staff, struck it once on the ground, and descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The mountains, rivers, and great earth; the grasses, trees, and forests—all are the number of thousands of Buddhas throughout kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Even if you can believe this to the point of total conviction, it is much like swinging a club to strike at the moon.
Buying high in the east and selling low in the west—where will you put your worn-out straw sandals after thirty years? You lacquer buckets, go to the meditation hall!"
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: A monk asked Master Youxi, "When the great function manifests before one, and no rules or patterns remain—what then?
Youxi rose, walked once around the meditation seat, and sat down. As the monk prepared to offer a word in response, Youxi gave him a kick.
The monk returned to his place and stood there. Youxi said, "You do so, but I do not; you do not do so, but I do. The monk...
He prepared to offer words of praise. Xiu then gave him another kick, saying, "Thirty years from now, my Way will flourish greatly.
The Master said, "A skilled archer does not shoot an arrow in vain. If one were truly such a man, where else would there be a 'Yu-xi' (Deep Creek)?
Nevertheless, as for that first kick at the beginning, how does it compare to this final kick? Try to examine this for yourself.
Ascending the hall for the Buddha-Bathing ceremony: From the beginning at Deer Park to the end at the Bahudā River, he exhausted his own mind and laughed the mouths of others to pieces.

As for the entrustment of the flower and the settling of the mind by Bodhidharma, the division into Northern and Southern schools, and the branching lineages of Caoxi—within the gate of the patch-robed monks, these are truly like digging the earth to seek the sky. (With the whisk, he draws a single stroke.)
It is precisely today, the anniversary of the birth of our Great Teacher, the Tathāgata. Throughout the world’s monasteries, this is celebrated once a year as the "Bathing of the Buddha.
If you call it the "Bathing of the Buddha," you are liable to receive a blow of the staff;
yet if you do not call it the "Bathing of the Buddha," you fail in gratitude and betray righteousness. Have you not seen how, when Zun the Nun was bathing the Buddha, Yaoshan asked her: "You only..."
“Zun was able to bathe this one, yet he could not bathe that one. Puna said, “Bring that one here! At this, Yaoshan simply withdrew.
The Master said, “If Zun Puna had been a true man at that time, when Yaoshan said, ‘I cannot bathe that one,’ he would have taken the ladle and flung it straight at his face.
Nevertheless, even so, he could not have failed to acknowledge Yaoshan. Why?”
"If you do not enter the tiger's den, how can you catch the tiger cub?

[The Master] ascended the hall and, citing Master Ciming, said: "Sometimes, inside his quarters, he would place a basin of water with a single-bladed sword resting across it and a pair of straw sandals beneath.
With a staff balanced horizontally upon his knees, whenever he saw a monk enter the door, he would simply point at him."
"As soon as he hesitated, [the Master] struck him with his staff. The Teacher said, "If I had been there at that time, I would have gone to his left ear and uttered a word very softly.
While he was distractedly gazing at the heavens, I would have pointed my finger. As soon as he hesitated, I would have drawn my sword and cut him down."
Suddenly picking up his staff, he descended from the seat, and the assembly dispersed all at once.
On the occasion of the opening of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall for a discourse. A monk asked, "All people fear the scorching heat; I love the length of the summer days.

When the fragrant breeze comes from the south and a slight coolness arises at the corner of the hall—what of it? The Master said, "Cast down the spears and lay aside the armor. The Master then took up his staff.

Holding [the staff] horizontally, he says: "I, the mountain-dwelling monk [Name], relying upon the Bodhisattva Vehicle, cultivate the practice of quiescence and enter together into the maintenance of the pure *dharmatā*.
Taking Great Perfect Enlightenment as my monastery, I dwell in peace within body and mind, abiding in the Wisdom of Equality."
Two thousand years ago, this old monk was with the twelve great bodhisattvas within the Treasury of Radiance, personally hearing the Tathāgata’s earnest oral entrustment.
Now, for the sake of sentient beings in the final age, he shall extensively expound this essential teaching.
This is precisely the time; out of gratitude, I dare not conceal it like a hidden treasure under my robes, but shall strike the eight characters for all of you once more.

He opened [the door] and departed. Striking the ground once with his staff, he said: "First, I invite the Great Being Mañjuśrī to recite the verse on the summer retreat for everyone from atop this mountain monk’s staff:
'To protect life, one must kill; only when all are killed does one truly enter the retreat.'"
If you wish to understand the meaning within this, an iron boat floats upon the water. Next, let the mountain monk once again speak a verse:
"Mañjuśrī seizes the tiger’s head; the mountain monk gathers the tiger’s tail. The bodhisattvas in between, standing in their ranks, give rise to joy."
Again, he struck the ground once with his staff and descended from the seat.
On the anniversary of the late Master of Tiger Hill, the Teacher held up incense and said: "In my life, I have had no luck; I have run into this old monk of no intelligence.
Though I exhausted every artifice, I could never reach him. From that time on, I laid down my weapons and, as best I could, donned the robe."
Wearing robes and eating rice; for twenty years he has sat upon a curved wooden seat, hanging up a goat’s head while selling dog meat.
What evidence does he have that others possess? Nevertheless, on this day when incense is burned once a year, it causes people’s resentment to deepen ever more profoundly through the ages.
Professor Yan was invited to ascend the hall. A monk asked, "If one remains unmoving in profound stillness, one brings disgrace upon the ancestral tradition;

if one manifests suddenly and expansively before oneself, one still fails one's own nature. Setting aside these two paths, how can one be 'just so'? The Master said, "A single blow and it is penetrated. The monk stepped forward and asked further.
The wind sweeps across the vast sky, and for a thousand *li* all is still; the sun’s orb stands at midday, and the eight directions are bright.

The Master said, "This is not yet where you, Venerable One, can let go of body and life. He stepped forward and asked, "It is just like when a monk asked Master Yangqi, 'What is the Buddha? and he replied:"
"A three-legged donkey prances about, pawing the ground. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Fools cannot be killed even by blows from a staff.
The student asked, "I do not understand where that third leg falls. The Master said, "You are drunk again.
The student asked, "If someone were to suddenly ask the Master, 'What is the Buddha? how would you answer him? The Master said, "I would strike him across the spine."
“Strike! The monk then bowed. The Master said, “A fellow who does not even recognize pain or itch. The Master then continued: “The meaning of the five hundred laborers lifting the rock:
walking with hands let go before a precipice ten thousand fathoms high. The entire world of the ten directions is a single mass of iron;
white fur grows upon the back of empty space. Even if you were to cast off your greasy cap and strip away your stinking cloth robe, [you would still be at] Baen.”
The members of the assembly are precisely those who deserve a blow of the staff. Why? Because at midnight they rise and sit with knees bent, and the Morning Star appears before the patch-robed monk.
Entering the hall:

Moving and stillness, going and coming—these are misuses of the mind. There is yet another place where the mind is misused, which I, Guizong, dare not reveal to you all.

"This is the wondrous function of spiritual powers; it is naturally so. The Master said, "One stroke, two pieces. The student asked, "The golden rooster pecks through the lapis lazuli shell; the jade hare pushes open the gate of the blue sea.

"What is Maitreya? The Master said, "It is nothing but a dried-up shit-stick.

The monk pressed further, "If that is so, then one must observe with great care and precision where it is manifested in every instance. The Master said, "You have no Buddha-nature; what would you observe? The monk bowed.
The Master then said: "Maitreya is truly Maitreya; he manifests a thousand, ten thousand, and a hundred million bodies.
From time to time he shows himself to those of this age, yet those of this age all fail to recognize him. This old fellow has now laid down his four legs squarely upon the ground.
Do you all recognize him yet? If you do recognize him, it is truly like adding grit to your eyes. If you do not recognize him, the fault lies with Baolin. [He then descended from the seat.]
Ascending the hall, he said: “When Bodhidharma came from the West, he pointed directly to the human mind, seeing one’s nature as becoming Buddha.
That old barbarian—if he had known at that time there was a ‘turning-over’ phrase, you all would not have avoided lying here with your corpses exposed and your bones bare! Now tell me:
when Baolin makes such an announcement, does he have any standing ground? Do not sit idly, waiting for the strange grass to turn green upon the cold crags.”

Xie Zhishi ascends the hall: "A single shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function proceed simultaneously. To understand the meaning within this," [one must look further].
At midday, they strike the watch of three. Consider this: before a single shout has even been uttered, are there guest and host?

Once they have been distinguished, which one is the guest and which one is the host? If you can discern this clearly here, then the guest shall remain the guest from beginning to end, and the host shall remain the host from beginning to end.
But what if the guest is not the guest and the host is not the host? Now, consider that single shout!
"Where does it land? Transversely grasping the Mohe sword, the true command is fully established; throughout the realm of Great Peace, the foolish and stubborn are executed.

Entering the hall, he said: "The authentic seal of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is the coarse, rugged state of the patch-robed monks. To have eyes yet be as if blind, to have a mouth yet be as if mute—if you ask further how it is, you may know that such conduct is beyond propriety."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: When a fellow practitioner arrived at Xinghua’s monastery and had just entered the Dharma Hall, Xinghua let out a shout.

The monk also shouted. Xinghua shouted again. The monk shouted once more. Xinghua stepped forward and brandished his staff. The monk shouted again. Xinghua said, "Look! This blind fellow still thinks he is the master.
As the monk hesitated, Xinghua struck him straight out of the Dharma Hall. A serving monk asked, "Regarding that monk just now..."
"What offense have I committed? Huachun replied, "That man just now had both the provisional and the real; he had both illumination and function.
When I held my hand out across his face twice, he could not proceed further. For a blind fellow like that, when would I wait to strike him?
If you ask why, Master Xinghua’s gate and walls are eight thousand feet high; this has always been our house."
The Dharma is solemn and severe. This monk has secretly penetrated the heavy barrier. If one wishes to see the spring colors within the cave, it is indeed fine;
yet, inevitably, both will suffer loss. As for Xinghua’s words, "I shall stretch my hand across his face twice"—what then?
Before heaven is established, hell is already formed.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Chan Master Anguo Ting. Once, when a monk asked the Fifth Patriarch, "What is the meaning of 'true nature giving rise to conditions'?

the Patriarch remained silent. At that time, Chan Master Ting was attending him and said, "Virtuous One, the very moment you give rise to a single thought—that is 'true nature giving rise to conditions' within true nature.
Upon these words, the monk attained great enlightenment. The Master remarked, "The Fifth Patriarch was not right to remain silent; it would have been better..."
"Twenty blows for giving the staff to Master Ting. Twenty blows for saying, 'Virtuous One, when you give rise to a single thought, that is dependent origination within true nature.
Twenty blows for the monk's failure to attain great enlightenment upon hearing these words.
Now tell me: did Baolin commit any fault? Twenty blows."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Layman Pang. One day, while selling his bamboo fish-trap, he tripped and fell to the ground.
Lingzhao immediately went and lay down beside him. The Layman asked, "What is this? Lingzhao said, "Seeing my father fall, I have come specifically to support you.
The Master said, "The Layman falls; Lingzhao helps him up. This is the mere skill of a beggar—what point is there in seeking its essence? He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The entire universe and the great earth, when gathered together, do not amount to even a single hair’s breadth.
Where, then, do you all establish yourselves and find your life? Even if you were to be bold and clear-sighted, you would still not escape binding yourself with no rope.
But tell me: in such a state, is there any place for exertion at Baolin? To cry until the blood flows is of no use; it is better to remain silent."

Now tell me: in what place does Guizong’s personhood reside? The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horns because it gazes at the moon; the elephant receives flowers within its tusks because it was startled by thunder.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: When Danxia visited National Teacher Zhong, he encountered the Teacher while he was sleeping.

He then asked the attendant, "Is the National Teacher here? The attendant replied, "He is indeed here; it is simply that he does not see guests. Danxia said, "How very remote! The attendant said, [Danxia's words were like this.]
"Do not speak of the Venerable Elder," [the Master said]. "Even with the Buddha-eye, one cannot see him. Xiangyun said, "The dragon begets dragon cubs; the phoenix begets phoenix chicks.
When the National Teacher woke from his sleep, the attendant reported this to him. The Teacher struck the attendant with twenty blows of the staff and drove him out of the monastery.
Dana heard it said: "He is not mistaken; he is the National Teacher of Nanyang. The Master said: "Attendant, eat the staff and leave the monastery. This is indeed a moment for a thousand years.
Yet how could Guizong avoid having his eyes burn with envy? Although Dana was indeed a skilled hand, alas, he fell into the National Teacher’s net.
Can you all discern this? If you have not yet realized it, it is like holding a golden whip while asking [for the horse].
Guests returning home: in the deep of night, who walks with you along the Imperial Street?

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Buddhas of the three periods, the six generations of patriarchs, the old monks throughout the world, the thirty-three heavens, and the twenty-eight lunar mansions—all are spending the summer retreat upon the tip of Guizong’s staff. [The Master] requested the head monk to preside over the assembly. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials;
as for the matter of the timing and conditions, what is it? The Master said, "A dog gnawing on a dry bone. The monk pressed further, "Linji addressed the assembly, saying:

[The student] said, "Born. The Master said, "An iron snake cannot penetrate it. [The student] further asked, "If someone were suddenly to come out and overturn the meditation seat, what then?
The Master said, "Draw the bow after the thief has gone. [The student] further asked, "I wonder, between these two people, which one is worthy of receiving offerings from devas and humans?
The Master said, "Neither is worthy. [The student] further asked, "Every person is fully endowed; each and every one..."

The Master said, "Da. The monk stepped forward and said, "Do not take offense at his haughty spirit; he has already trodden upon the highest pass. The Master said, "You have been killed by me, Da."

Jìn said, "Once the shout has been let fall, the paths of mud and water are distinguished; who knows the message within this?"
The Master asked, "What is the sword that kills? The monk said, "It is already before words. The Master said, "When did you ever speak of it? The Master then said:
"In the past, the venerable elders who served the Dharma never grew weary of supporting the assembly.
How much more so now, as I have grown frail with age; my movements often conflict with what is required. You must deeply reflect upon the affairs of your entire life and apply yourself."
Open your mind and uphold this well; if you can ensure that not even a single grain leaks away, then the Shaolin tradition will not be separated from you by so much as a hair’s breadth.

Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: Once, when Danxia passed through a monastery during a severe freeze, he saw a wooden Buddha in the main hall.
He took it up, lit a fire, and burned it. By chance, the monastery superintendent saw this and rebuked him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden Buddha?

Danxia struck the ashes with his staff and said, "I am burning for the sake of the *śarīra*. The superintendent said, "A wooden Buddha—how could it have *śarīra*? Danxia replied, "Since there are none..."
"Śāriputra, please invite two more statues; take them again and burn them. Thereafter, the abbot’s eyebrows and beard fell out.
The Master said, "The practitioners of various quarters speculate that this calamity occurred because the abbot suddenly gave rise to a doubting mind.

Others say it was because the abbot did not give Danxia fire when it was cold, thereby causing the wooden Buddha to be burned, which resulted in his eyebrows and beard falling out. This is quite different [from the truth]."
[The Master said: "I do not know. The head monk bought iron and obtained gold;

Xinghua said, "Strike the one in the center. The monk then bowed. Xinghua said, "Yesterday I attended a village feast; on the way back, I encountered a sudden storm..."
"A wind, rain, and storm—[we] were able to take shelter inside an ancient temple. The Master said:

"Among the assembly, some deliberate, saying that being able to take shelter inside an ancient temple clarifies the self prior to the kalpa of emptiness; others say it is precisely where he establishes his dwelling and sustains his life.
Little do they realize that Xinghua was girded with a hundred thousand strings of cash as he rode a crane down to Yangzhou."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "At Vulture Peak, the flower was held up; at Shaolin, the direct pointing was given. Pointing at emptiness and painting emptiness is like washing soil in mud.
As for the Buddha-dharma (Tathāgata-citta), a white lotus blooms amidst the glare of a blazing fire. As for the Patriarch’s intent, red dust rises in billowing clouds from the bottom of the sea.

If you can penetrate through this, you will shatter the provisional and the real, as well as illumination and function, with a single blow of the hammer. If you cannot penetrate through, you will sit in meditation for years within a thicket of entanglements."
It is not like that at all. "Bring out the blind donkey to pull the millstone!
Ascending the hall, he raised a passage from the teachings which says: "Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—these three are without distinction. The Master said:
"Thirty years ago, when I heard such words, I laughed and could not stop. Thirty years later, hearing such words, I am filled with joy."
I cannot sleep. You people here—having heard Donglin speak thus—have you been able to distinguish the black from the white?
If you have not been able to distinguish them, listen to this verse: "The mind, the Buddha, and sentient beings— Laughing, they return to joy.

This laughter and joy have no root; Yet the distinction between black and white truly has its purpose. Of all those who have lived through the ages, How many truly understand the principle? The principle is profound."
"Where do you seek it? He suddenly picked up his staff, struck it once, and said: "When the ocean dries up, its bottom will finally be seen;
when a person dies, their mind is not known. Ascending the hall, he raised an old case: A monk asked Yunmen, "Within the three virtues and six flavors, is there still any Buddha-dharma or not?
Yunmen said, "I only fear that you would not ask. The monk said, "Please, Master, speak. Yunmen said, "The three virtues and six flavors are bestowed upon the Buddhas and..."
The monk said, "Master Yunmen did not fail that monk who came to question him; he could not avoid falling into a pitfall.
If you all can understand it here, I grant you the right to stride across the crown of Vairocana.

When the Master entered the temple and ascended the hall, he held up the incense and said:

"This one offering of incense is respectfully offered to the present Emperor to pray for his sacred longevity—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years. He then held up the incense again and said:

"This single offering of incense is respectfully offered for the Chancellor, Pacifier, and Imperial Resident, the State Councilor and Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, as well as all the meritorious nobles of the province, to collectively augment their years of office and longevity. He then picked up the incense again and said:

"This is respectfully offered for the late Abbot of Mount Huqiu in Pingjiang Prefecture, the Venerable Master Long, to repay the kindness of his Dharma-milk. Thereupon, he adjusted his robes and took his seat. The Abbot of Baoning addressed the assembly.
The Master struck the sounding block and said, "In this Dharma assembly, you dragons and elephants, you should contemplate the primary truth (*paramārtha*).

The Master continued, "If one speaks of the primary truth, it is like a single speck of snow upon a red-hot furnace. If you cannot hear beyond sound and see beyond form, what prevents you from coming forward from the assembly to resolve your doubts?
A monk asked, "The ancient Śākyamuni was not first; the new Maitreya will not be last. It is precisely today."
"The Buddha-dharma has been entrusted to Mount Jiangshan. I do not know how to proclaim that pivotal function which the thousand sages did not borrow.
How should one raise it? The Master said, "Realize it directly. The monk said, "In that case, one controls the great pivot of the Buddhas and patriarchs and expands the true eye of humans and devas.
The Master said, "It pierces the nostrils of all monks under heaven. The monk said, "A single phrase transcends the standards of past and present; ten thousand years shall look up to it."

[The monk] offered congratulations to the Sage and Enlightened Ruler. The Master said, "He speaks it with his whole mouth. The monk asked, "As for that pivot which does not borrow, how can it be transmitted?
The Master said, "Look behind the head. The monk said, "With copper heads and iron jaws like dragons and tigers, look at the golden circle and the thorny *liji* fruit.
The Master said, "That is precisely what I, this old monk, employ. The monk said, "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, the World-Honored One..."
When the Flower was held up, Kāśyapa smiled. I do not yet know what this meaning is. The Master said, "One person transmits the empty;
ten thousand people transmit the real. The monk said, "The World-Honored One said: 'I have the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye; I entrust it to Mahākāśyapa.'"
"Furthermore, how is it? The Master said, "Hearing things not clearly, one calls a bell a jar. The monk asked, "At Mount Ling, the Flower was held up to entrust the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye;
today at Jiangshan, as the hall is opened, what instruction do you have to offer? The Master said, "Do you see it yet?
The monk said, "Today’s assembly is no different from that at Mount Ling. The Master said, "Try to go beyond that by even a single step. The monk—

"The true body of the Vajra encompasses the ten voids; penetrating from top to bottom, it is beyond all entanglement;
spanning from antiquity to the present, it has no front or back; it is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing. Seizing the head and cutting it off—ten thousand [things are thus resolved]."
The eyes suddenly open. Heaven and earth attain harmony through this; the myriad phenomena attain brilliance through this; the Buddhas appear in the world through this;

the Patriarchs come from the West through this; and monks establish the field for selecting Buddhas through this, opening the great furnace and bellows, wielding the tongs and hammers of their own true portion, and shattering the nests of false teachers. Within this midst, one or two individuals descend like clouds.
Head. Once one realizes what is not [the truth], one will clearly penetrate that great matter prior to the arising of Buddhas; it does not depend on a single moment.
One suddenly enters the inconceivable gate of great liberation—what is called a Great Man accomplishing the deeds of a Great Man.
Therefore, at the assembly on Vulture Peak, the butcher Guang'e cast down his butcher’s blade and said, "I am one of the thousand Buddhas."

First, regarding the number: within the Great Assembly, the powerful Māra King said, "I shall wait until all sentient beings have fully attained Buddhahood and the realm of sentient beings is emptied;
only then will I resolve to attain Bodhicitta. Is this not like a dragon galloping or a tiger charging, or like a fragrant elephant crossing a river?
It is also like a lute made of lion sinew: when it is played, all other sounds are instantly silenced. When one reaches this point, there is nothing above.
Climbing upward, one reaches for the heights; looking downward, one cuts off one's own body. The constant light manifests before one; standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.

On the occasion of the New Year’s Hall discourse: "The New Year begins its reign; there is no room for evasion. All things are renewed; it cuts through iron and severs nails."
Receiving blessings at the opportune moment, one leaps out of the old molds. "The early spring is still cold"—words are upright and speech is upright.

After a long silence, he said: "The Great Man above, Qiu Yi Ji."

Therefore, by the power of his original vow, he tirelessly rescues sentient beings. Yunmen could not restrain his impatience and struck [the Buddha], saying, 'Let the dog eat it! What is the meaning of this?"
Profound and secret; it cannot be reached by speech or silence. On the eighth day of the fourth month, this was the site of his birth.

Huangbo asked, 'What are you doing planting so many pines in the deep mountains? Linji replied, 'First, to provide a scenic setting for the mountain gate;
second, to serve as a landmark for future generations. Having spoken, he struck the ground three times with his mattock. Huangbo said, 'Even so, you have already been bitten.'"
"I have received thirty blows. Linji then struck the ground three times and made a whistling sound. Huangbo said, "My lineage will flourish greatly in the world through you.
Later, Guishan asked Yangshan, "At that time, Huangbo entrusted his lineage to Linji alone;
was there anyone else? Yangshan replied, "There were others, but because the years have passed so long, I do not wish to mention them to you, Master."
Miaoyan said, "Even so, I still wish to know. Just bring it up and let me see. Yangshan said, "There is a man who points toward Wu and Yue and causes his commands to be carried out;
yet when he encounters a great wind, he stops. The Master said, "Huangbo said, 'Even so, you have already received thirty blows from me.

"Go! It is a pity that you would willingly bury yourself alive by the side of a hoe. Yangshan’s understanding has not yet emerged from the common flow;
it is not merely a case of stopping when encountering a great wind. Why did he not say at that time: 'Wait until the realm of empty space is exhausted, and only then will this talk begin to spread'?

Is this not a case of being straight from head to tail? Today, Jiangshan pulls back his face-skin, wishing to give [him]— [Note: The provided text ends abruptly. The translation reflects the available portion.]

to oppose the superior, there is none other than the lion’s cub."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Before the fifteenth day, it is half dark and half light; after the fifteenth day, it is half light and half dark.
On the fifteenth day itself, his face is like the full moon and his eyes are like lotuses; gods and humans alike pay him reverence."
When an arrow strikes a mulberry tree, sap flows from a willow tree. If we discuss the two characters of the Buddha-dharma, it is like Xie San-niang selling silver.
Chan Master Dahui of Jingshan arrived; he ascended the hall. A monk asked: "In the past, when Fahua visited Langya, both of them raised the supreme mechanism to manifest extraordinary matters.
Today, Jingshan’s majestic carriage has graced us with its presence; I wonder how you will respond?"

They met face to face. The Master said, "Two lacquer buckets rubbing against each other. The student advanced and said, "Within the sphere of a person of thorough penetration, one encounters [the truth] at every turn.
The Master said, "By all means, do not understand it in that way. The student said, "Not only has the Master personally seen and heard this;

for us students, the multitude, it is a small emergence meeting with a great encounter. The Master said, "Everyone will fall into pits and ravines. The student said, "It reaches the point where the ancient wind comes without ceasing."

[The student] looked up and said, "The Buddha-sun is shining at its zenith. The Master said, "He has spoken it from his full mouth. [The student] asked, "If the mind is not the Buddha and wisdom is not the Way, then what?
The Master said, "Dig a deep hole and bury him. [The student] asked, "Is there still a place for one to take responsibility?
The Master said, "By all means, avoid taking responsibility. [The student] said, "A staff strikes the head of a stone man; let us strip away the husk to discuss the reality."
The Master asked, "What is the reality? The monk said, "The subsequent text is long. The Master said, "Quickly prostrate three times.
The monk said, "I thank the Master for his reply. The Master then said, "I originally had no mind to seek anything;
now this great jewel of the Dharma King has arrived of its own accord. Since the great jewel of the Dharma King has arrived, you all must urgently apply yourselves with diligence."
This is truly so. It is said: "If you do not take it when you see it, it will be a thousand miles away when you think of it. Have you not heard the words of the Great Sui Monk?

The Master is but one person. With his black-lacquered bamboo whisk, he overturns the seas and mountains, striking from head to toe;
though it may seem like treating a dead horse, therein lies the subtle mystery. When Huangbo struck Linji with his staff, did Jiangshan lack such a tool?

The monk stumbled while walking on the road and attained a moment of realization. Upon returning, he reported this to his master. Later, the master appointed him as the guest prefect (*kṣāntivādin*).

He suddenly grasped his staff, struck it once, and said: "Everyone is invited to enter here! To realize the Way through hearing sound, and to clarify the mind through seeing form—this is Avalokiteśvara."
A Bodhisattva was about to buy some sesame cakes with his money; when he let it go, it turned out to be a mere deception.
Again, he took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "If you enter here, you will blind people's eyes; if you do not enter here, where else will you enter?
A person of keen faculties turns at a single push, yet they must further know the path by which one emerges. I dare ask:"
"Great assembly, what is the single path for manifesting one's true self? He then struck the ground once and said, "Lift your heads and look beyond the heavens;
who else is there like me?"
Ascending the hall on the first day of the First Month: Last year there was no such snow; this year there is this snow.

A single expanse of pure light rests in profound stillness.
[The Master] ascends the hall and says: A monk once asked Duofu, "What is Duofu’s grove of bamboo? Duofu replied, "One stalk, two stalks, leaning. The monk said, "I do not understand.

Those who cross the seas and climb the mountains are all equally blessed by his rain and dew. Śākyamuni and Maitreya together rejoice in this era of peace; Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra alike propagate the True Teaching. In every atom and every world-system..."
